mainTopic: End of the נבוכדנצר אגדה, then the משנה on arranging weekday matters on שבת: hinting versus speaking, speech versus thought, and permitted talk about חפצי שמים and calculations.
overview: This amud first finishes the אגדה about נבוכדנצר and בבל: two readings of a verse about בבל's greed for gold, and a teaching that נבוכדנצר even ruled over wild beasts. A new משנה then forbids hiring workers on שבת, asking someone else to hire them, or waiting at the edge of the תחום in order to hire workers or bring produce. Waiting there in order to guard produce is allowed. אבא שאול sums it up: whatever I may talk about on שבת, I may wait at the תחום for. The גמרא asks why the משנה mentions 'his friend' at all. After רב פפא's answer (the friend is a גוי) is rejected, רב אשי explains that the clause implies a hint like 'will you join me this evening?' is permitted. That is the view of רבי יהושע בן קרחה, and the הלכה follows him. רבי יוחנן derives it from the פסוק 'ודבר דבר': speaking is forbidden, but thinking is allowed. A side discussion squares this with the ban on thinking Torah in a bathroom, and with רב יהודה's rule against reciting קריאת שמע before a naked גוי. Finally the גמרא shows that talk about מצוה and community matters is permitted, because only 'your business' is forbidden, not חפצי שמים. It then begins to discuss which calculations are permitted on שבת, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two readings of the nation that demanded gold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes one reading of the verse about בבל ('measure and bring') and then gives a second reading ('bring a lot, without measure').
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Measure and bring.' And some say the nation said: 'Bring very, very much, without measuring.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an explanation it started on the previous page. A verse in ישעיהו describes בבל, and the גמרא explains it in two ways: בבל demanded measured tribute, or בבל demanded endless gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse's unusual word מַדְהֵבָה is read as a wordplay. The first view reads it as מְדוֹד וְהָבֵא, 'measure and bring,' meaning strict measured tribute. The second view, introduced with וְאִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי, reads it as מְאֹד מְאֹד הָבֵא, 'bring very much,' meaning greed without any limit.

keyTerms.meaning: Measure and bring. This is one wordplay reading of the verse.
And some say. This introduces an alternative version or opinion.
Without measure, meaning with no limit.

phrases.english: Measure and bring.
phrases.notes: The end of the first explanation, which began on the previous page.

phrases.english: And some say
phrases.notes: Here comes a second way of explaining it.

phrases.english: that it said: 'Bring very, very much, without measure.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues an aggadic exposition from the previous page and offers an alternative reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The verse describes בבל's greed for gold. In one reading it demanded measured tribute; in the other it demanded unlimited wealth.

steps.title: נבוכדנצר rode a lion with a serpent tied on its head
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב ירמיה בר אבא, explains the verse in דניאל about נבוכדנצר's extra greatness: he even ruled over wild beasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And extra greatness was added to me.' רב יהודה said in the name of רב ירמיה בר אבא: this teaches that he rode on a male lion and tied a serpent to its head. This fulfilled the verse: 'Even the beasts of the field I have given him to serve him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another verse about נבוכדנצר. It explains that his 'extra greatness' means he controlled even dangerous animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'extra greatness' in דניאל is given a concrete meaning: power over wild animals. The verse from ירמיהו is used to show that this was a fulfillment of a prophecy. With this, the aggadic section closes, and the next step begins a new משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Extra greatness, an Aramaic phrase from דניאל.

phrases.english: 'And extra greatness was added to me,'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said:
this teaches that he rode on a male lion,
and tied a serpent to its head,
to fulfill what is said:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְגַם אֶת חַיַּת הַשָּׂדֶה נָתַתִּי לוֹ לְעׇבְדוֹ״.
phrases.english: 'And also the beasts of the field I have given him to serve him.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another aggadic teaching about נבוכדנצר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Extra greatness' means נבוכדנצר ruled even over wild animals, fulfilling the prophecy in ירמיהו.

steps.title: No hiring workers on שבת, not even through a friend
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens. One may not hire workers on שבת, and one may not tell another person to hire workers for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person may not hire workers on שבת. And a person may not tell his friend to hire workers for him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It forbids arranging to hire workers on שבת, whether you do it yourself or ask someone else to do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The workers will not work on שבת itself. Even so, arranging weekday business by speaking about it on שבת is forbidden. The second clause, about telling 'his friend,' is the line the גמרא will soon question as seemingly obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה: the start of the משנה text.
To his friend, meaning another person.

steps.confusionAlert: The workers are not being hired to work on שבת. They will work after שבת. The prohibition is on making the arrangement, the talking and hiring, on שבת itself.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A person may not hire workers on Shabbat.
And a person may not tell his friend
to hire workers for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ לֹא יִשְׂכּוֹר אָדָם פּוֹעֲלִים בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new halachic topic after the aggadah ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hiring workers on שבת is forbidden, both directly and by asking another person to do it.

steps.title: Waiting at the boundary: forbidden for hiring, allowed for guarding
steps.stepSummary: One may not wait at the edge of the תחום שבת in order to hire workers or bring produce after שבת. One may wait there in order to guard produce, and he may then carry produce back.
steps.simpleTranslation: We may not wait for dark at the boundary in order to hire workers or bring produce. But he may wait for dark in order to guard, and then he may bring produce back in his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה discusses מחשיכין על התחום: waiting at the edge of the שבת boundary so you can set out the moment שבת ends. Whether this is allowed depends on what you plan to do once שבת is over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hiring workers and bringing produce are things you could not even discuss on שבת, so waiting for them is forbidden. Guarding produce is permitted, because one could guard it on שבת if it were inside the boundary. Once he goes out to guard, he may also bring produce back, since that was not his original reason for waiting.

keyTerms.meaning: Waiting for nightfall, so that one can leave right as שבת ends.
The שבת boundary, about 2000 אמות from town.

phrases.english: We may not wait for nightfall at the Shabbat boundary
to hire workers for himself or to bring produce,
but he may wait for nightfall in order to guard,
and he may bring produce back in his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the ban on arranging weekday matters to waiting at the boundary.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Waiting at the תחום to hire workers or bring produce is forbidden. Waiting to guard is allowed, and produce may be carried back incidentally.

steps.title: אבא שאול's general rule
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול gives a general principle: whatever I am allowed to talk about on שבת, I may also wait at the boundary for.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול said a general rule: anything I am allowed to say on שבת, I am allowed to wait for dark at the boundary for it.
steps.whatsHappening: אבא שאול sums up the משנה with one principle that ties waiting at the boundary to speaking on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Speech and waiting are linked. If you may say something on שבת, you may also wait at the boundary to do it after שבת. This explains why guarding is allowed and hiring workers is not.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted to say it, meaning to speak about it.

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of the משנה: what you may say on שבת, you may wait at the תחום for. What you may not say, you may not wait for.

phrases.english: Abba Shaul stated a general rule:
anything that I am permitted to say —
I am permitted to wait for nightfall at the boundary for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Generalizes the cases of the משנה into one principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Permission to wait at the תחום for something follows permission to speak about it on שבת.

steps.title: Why mention the friend at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say one may not tell a friend to hire workers. That seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It is obvious! What is the difference between him and his friend?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the משנה. If hiring workers on שבת is forbidden for me, it is surely forbidden for my Jewish friend too, so why say it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is that the second clause adds nothing. A Jewish friend is under the same prohibition, so telling him to hire is clearly also forbidden. The משנה should not need to spell this out.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא: the start of the גמרא's discussion.
It is obvious. This challenges a statement as unnecessary.

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: פְּשִׁיטָא מַאי שְׁנָא הוּא וּמַאי שְׁנָא חֲבֵירוֹ?
phrases.english: It is obvious! What is the difference between him and his friend?

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא מַאי שְׁנָא הוּא וּמַאי שְׁנָא חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the first clauses of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's clause 'and a person may not tell his friend to hire workers for him.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The clause seems redundant, because a Jewish friend is equally forbidden to hire on שבת.

steps.title: רב פפא: the 'friend' is a גוי
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the 'friend' in the משנה refers to a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: the friend is a גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question by reinterpreting the word 'friend.' It does not mean a Jew; it means a non-Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the friend were a Jew, the clause would be obvious. If the friend is a גוי, who is not commanded to keep שבת, the משנה is teaching something new: you still may not ask him to hire workers for you.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The friend is a gentile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a term in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'friend' is a Jew, which would make the clause obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'friend' is a גוי, so the clause teaches that even asking a non-Jew is forbidden.

steps.title: רב אשי: telling a גוי is already a known שבות
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי objects that telling a גוי to do forbidden work is already a known rabbinic prohibition, so רב פפא's answer leaves the clause just as obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי challenged this: telling a גוי is a שבות!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks רב פפא's answer. Everyone already knows that אמירה לנכרי is forbidden on שבת, so the משנה still seems to be teaching nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's goal was to make the clause say something new. רב אשי argues that the general ban on asking a non-Jew to do work for you on שבת already covers this case. So the original problem of redundancy comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Telling a non-Jew to do a forbidden act for a Jew on שבת.

steps.whyThisMatters: This objection makes רב אשי drop the גוי reading entirely. In the next step he explains the clause differently, keeping 'his friend' as a Jew.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi strongly objected to this:
Telling a gentile is a rabbinic prohibition!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's answer in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that the 'friend' is a גוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אמירה לנכרי is already known to be a שבות, so reading the clause as referring to a גוי still leaves it redundant.

steps.title: רב אשי's own answer: the clause teaches that hinting is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the friend may be a Jew. The משנה's wording implies that an open request is forbidden but a hinting question is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: even if the 'friend' is a Jew, the משנה teaches this. You may not say 'hire workers for me', but you may say 'Do you think you'll join me this evening?'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejected רב פפא's answer in the last step. Now he gives his own reason why the משנה needed this clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is not the obvious ban on asking someone to hire workers. The new point is what the משנה leaves out. Only a direct request is banned, so a hinting question about working together after שבת is allowed, even when both people understand what is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say (you can keep the simple reading)
This is what it comes to teach us
Hire workers for me (a direct request)
Do you think you'll join me this evening? (a hint)

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying the 'hire workers' ban itself is new. The חידוש comes from the contrast: a direct request is forbidden, but a hint is permitted.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
Even if you say 'his friend' means a Jew,
this is what it teaches us:
A person may not say to his friend
"Hire workers for me,"
but a person may say to his friend
"Does it seem that you will join me this evening?"

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא חֲבֵירוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב פפא's answer, which רב אשי rejected in step 8, with a new explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the clause's purpose: the חידוש is the implied permission, not the stated prohibition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The clause seemed to state something obvious, and רב פפא's answer did not fix that.
steps.terutzMaskana: The clause teaches by implication that hinting at future work is permitted on שבת.

steps.title: Whose view does the משנה follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא the משנה follows, given רב אשי's reading. It answers: רבי יהושע בן קרחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And whose view is our משנה? It follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies who holds that hinting is allowed. This sets up the proof from a ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the משנה is read as permitting a hint, it must belong to a תנא who allows this. The גמרא names him as רבי יהושע בן קרחה.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, whose view is it?
The תנא who permits hinting on שבת

phrases.english: And our Mishnah, whose view is it?
It is like Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies which תנא holds the view that רב אשי reads into the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's opinion does the משנה follow, under רב אשי's reading?

steps.title: The ברייתא where the hint question is disputed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a dispute. The first opinion forbids asking 'will you join me this evening?' and רבי יהושע בן קרחה permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: a person may not say to his friend 'Do you think you'll join me this evening?' רבי יהושע בן קרחה says: a person may say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that the hinting question is actually a dispute, and that רבי יהושע בן קרחה is the one who allows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that רב אשי's reading is not obvious. The first, anonymous opinion forbids even a hint. So the משנה's implied permission matches רבי יהושע בן קרחה specifically.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: As it was taught:
A person may not say to his friend
"Does it seem that you will join me this evening?"
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha says:
A person may say to his friend
"Does it seem that you will join me this evening?"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source showing that רבי יהושע בן קרחה permits the hint.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה, as רב אשי reads it, follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the dispute about the hinting question.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that the הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן decides the dispute: hinting like this is allowed on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns the ברייתא's dispute into practical law. One may ask 'will you join me this evening?' on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of
An אמורא who reports רבי יוחנן's statements

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling: a hint about work after שבת is permitted, even though a direct request is not.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the dispute from the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה, so the hinting question is permitted on שבת.

steps.title: The reason: speaking is forbidden, thinking is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains רבי יהושע בן קרחה's reason. The פסוק says 'וְדַבֵּר דָּבָר' (speaking a word), so only speaking about weekday matters is forbidden, while thinking about them is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן also said: what is רבי יהושע בן קרחה's reason? The פסוק says 'from pursuing your business and speaking a word.' Speaking is forbidden; thinking is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the source in the פסוק for permitting the hint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ישעיה forbids weekday talk on שבת. Since it says 'speaking', only actual speech about business is forbidden, and thought is not included. A hint does not openly state the business, so it does not count as forbidden speech.

keyTerms.meaning: From pursuing your business and speaking a word (ישעיה נח:יג)

steps.whatToRemember: On שבת, speaking about weekday business is forbidden (דיבור אסור), but thinking about it is allowed (הרהור מותר).

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabba bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה —
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha?
As it is written: "From pursuing your business and speaking a word."
Speaking is forbidden; thinking is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the ruling in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Based on the פסוק, speech about weekday matters is forbidden on שבת, but thought is not.

steps.title: Contradiction: רבי יוחנן forbids thinking Torah in a bathroom
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר רב הונא asks רבא how רבי יוחנן can say thinking is not like speaking. רבי יוחנן also said one may think Torah anywhere except a bathhouse or bathroom, which implies thinking is like speaking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר רב הונא raised a contradiction to רבא: did רבי יוחנן really say that speaking is forbidden but thinking is allowed, meaning thought is not like speech? But רבי יוחנן said: one may think Torah anywhere except a bathhouse and a bathroom!
steps.whatsHappening: Two statements of רבי יוחנן are set against each other. One says thought does not count, and the other seems to treat thought as forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If thought were never like speech, thinking Torah in a bathroom should be allowed, just as speaking Torah there is banned but thinking would be fine. Since רבי יוחנן forbids even thinking there, he seems to hold that thought counts like speech, which contradicts step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a contradiction to him

phrases.aramaic: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Rav Huna raised a contradiction to Rava:
Did Rabbi Yochanan really say
speaking is forbidden, thinking is permitted?
This shows that thinking is not like speaking.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: But Rabba bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
In every place it is permitted to think (Torah),
except in a bathhouse and a bathroom!

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the principle from step 13 using another statement of the same אמורא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's principle that thought is not like speech.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן forbids even thinking Torah in a bathroom, which implies that thought does count like speech. His two statements contradict each other.

steps.title: Bathroom case is different: the camp must be holy
steps.stepSummary: The bathroom rule comes from a different source, 'וְהָיָה מַחֲנֶיךָ קָדוֹשׁ' (your camp shall be holy). Thinking Torah in a dirty place breaks that holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because we need 'your camp shall be holy,' and that is missing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. The bathroom rule is not about 'speech versus thought' at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on Torah in a bathroom comes from the requirement of holiness. Even thinking Torah in a filthy place is a lack of holiness. So the bathroom rule does not prove that thought equals speech in general, and the שבת rule stays as it was.

keyTerms.meaning: Your camp shall be holy (דברים כג:טו)

phrases.english: It is different there,
since we require "your camp shall be holy,"
and that is lacking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the sources: the bathroom rule is based on holiness, not on speech.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Forbidding thought in a bathroom shows that thought is generally like speech.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bathroom rule comes from the requirement of holiness, so it says nothing about thought versus speech in general.

steps.title: But that same verse says 'דבר', implying speech
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. The same פסוק continues 'וְלֹא יִרְאֶה בְךָ עֶרְוַת דָּבָר'. The word דבר hints at speech (דיבור), which would mean only speech is banned in a bathroom.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too it is written: 'So that He not see in you an unseemly thing (דבר)'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 15, using the next words of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'דבר' sounds like 'דיבור', speech. Then this פסוק itself would limit the bathroom ban to speaking, and thinking Torah there should be allowed. That clashes with רבי יוחנן's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: An unseemly thing (with 'דבר' read as hinting at speech)

phrases.english: Here too, it is written:
"So that He not see in you an unseemly thing (davar)"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from step 15 using the continuation of the same פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the bathroom ban is based on holiness and so includes thought.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק's word 'דבר' implies speech, so the bathroom ban should cover only speaking, like the שבת rule.

steps.title: That verse is needed for רב יהודה's rule about nakedness
steps.stepSummary: The words 'ערות דבר' are needed for a different law, taught by רב יהודה. One may not recite קריאת שמע facing a naked גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק is needed for רב יהודה's teaching. רב יהודה said: facing a naked גוי, it is forbidden to recite קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The phrase 'ערות דבר' is about nakedness, not about speech.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase is used to teach that one may not recite קריאת שמע in front of an exposed person. Since it is used for that law, it cannot also limit the bathroom ban to speech. So 'your camp shall be holy' still bans even thinking Torah in a bathroom, and there is no contradiction with the שבת rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (a different teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's two rules fit together. On שבת, speech about business is forbidden and thought is allowed, based on 'ודבר דבר'. Torah thought in a bathroom is forbidden because of holiness, based on 'והיה מחניך קדוש'. 'ערות דבר' teaches רב יהודה's law about nakedness.

phrases.english: That verse is needed for the teaching of Rav Yehuda.
For Rav Yehuda said:
Facing a naked non-Jew,
it is forbidden to recite Shema opposite him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16 by showing that the phrase 'ערות דבר' is used for a different law.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirecting the פסוק: the phrase is needed for another law, so no inference about speech can be drawn from it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'דבר' limits the bathroom ban to speech.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ערות דבר' teaches רב יהודה's ban on reciting שמע facing nakedness. The holiness requirement still bans even thinking Torah in a bathroom.

steps.title: Why mention a non-Jew specifically?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב יהודה said 'facing a naked גוי' when facing a naked ישראל is just as forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why specifically a גוי? Even a Jew is also forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the wording of רב יהודה's rule from the last step. Why did he mention only a naked גוי?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If reciting קריאת שמע facing nakedness is forbidden, the rule should apply to any naked person. Naming a גוי makes it sound like a Jew might be different. So the גמרא asks what that detail adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically? (asks why one case was chosen)

phrases.english: Why specifically a gentile?
phrases.notes: Refers to רב יהודה's rule in step 17.

phrases.english: Even a Jew is also forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִירְיָא גּוֹי, אֲפִילּוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the specific wording of רב יהודה's rule quoted in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's choice to mention a גוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule seems to apply equally to a Jew, so mentioning a גוי looks unnecessary or misleading.

steps.title: The non-Jew case is the bigger חידוש
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה used the 'לא מיבעיא' style. A Jew is obviously forbidden. He needed to teach that even a גוי counts, despite a פסוק comparing their flesh to donkeys.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is speaking in the style of 'there is no need to say.' There is no need to say a Jew is forbidden. But about a גוי, since it is written 'whose flesh is like the flesh of donkeys,' I might say it is fine. So he teaches us it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב יהודה chose the less obvious case on purpose. It teaches that even a גוי's nakedness counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in יחזקאל compares a גוי's flesh to a donkey's flesh. That might suggest it does not count as 'ערוה.' רב יהודה teaches the surprising case, and the obvious case of a Jew is included automatically.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no need to say (the obvious case is assumed)

steps.confusionAlert: The 'לא מיבעיא' style does not mean the Jewish case is less strict. It means the Jewish case is so obvious that it did not need to be said.

phrases.english: He is speaking in the style of 'there is no need'
There is no need to say a Jew, that it is forbidden
But a gentile, since it is written about him:
'Whose flesh is the flesh of donkeys'
I might say it is fine
So he teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: לא מיבעיא: the less obvious case was stated to teach a new point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of the פסוק comparing them to donkeys, a גוי's nakedness might not count as ערוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a גוי's nakedness counts. A Jew's obviously does.

steps.title: Maybe a non-Jew's nakedness really doesn't count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. Perhaps the 'donkey' פסוק really does mean a גוי's body is not ערוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it is indeed so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. Why not take the 'donkey' פסוק at face value and say a naked גוי is allowed?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 gave the 'donkey' idea only as a mistaken assumption. Here the גמרא asks for a reason to reject it. Without a source, maybe the assumption is correct.

phrases.english: Say it is indeed so (that it is permitted)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption in step 19 that a גוי's nakedness counts.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a גוי's nakedness counts as ערוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק in יחזקאל seems to support treating it as not ערוה, so why reject that reading?

steps.title: נח's nakedness is called ערוה
steps.stepSummary: The תורה calls נח's body 'ערות אביהם,' and נח was not Jewish. So a non-Jew's body is ערוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And they did not see their father's nakedness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves from a פסוק that a non-Jew's body is called ערוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שם and יפת covered their father נח and 'did not see their father's ערוה.' נח lived before מתן תורה, so he was a בן נח, not a Jew. Since the תורה calls his body ערוה, a גוי's nakedness counts.
steps.whatToRemember: Reciting קריאת שמע facing any naked person, Jew or non-Jew, is forbidden. The proof is that the תורה calls נח's body ערוה.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'And they did not see their father's nakedness.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: וְעֶרְוַת אֲבִיהֶם לֹא רָאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20 with a פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גוי's body might not be ערוה because of the 'donkey' פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה calls נח's body ערוה, so a non-Jew's nakedness counts.

steps.title: Many sources allow speaking about plans on שבת
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the main topic, the גמרא asks whether speaking about weekday matters is really forbidden on שבת. Many teachings allow planning and arranging things on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is speaking really forbidden? רב חסדא and רב המנונא both said: calculations for a מצוה may be made on שבת. רבי אלעזר said: one may set charity amounts for the poor on שבת. רבי יוחנן said: one may arrange life-saving matters and community needs on שבת, and go to בתי כנסיות to handle community matters. רבי יוחנן also said: one may go to theaters, circuses, and courthouses to handle community matters on שבת. The school of מנשה taught: one may arrange matches for children on שבת, and arrange for a child to learn to read and learn a trade.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the bathroom side topic and goes back to the rule from step 13, that speaking about weekday matters is forbidden on שבת. It brings a list of sources that seem to allow such talk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All these activities involve talking about money, deals, or arrangements, which looks like 'weekday speech.' If such speech were forbidden, these rulings could not stand. So the rule from step 13 seems to be contradicted.

phrases.english: And is speaking really forbidden?
phrases.notes: This goes back to step 13, about weekday talk on שבת.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַב הַמְנוּנָא דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: But Rav Chisda and Rav Hamnuna both said:
Calculations of a מצוה
are permitted to calculate on Shabbat.
And Rabbi Elazar said:
One may allocate charity for the poor on Shabbat.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:

phrases.aramaic: מְפַקְּחִין פִּיקּוּחַ נֶפֶשׁ וּפִיקּוּחַ רַבִּים בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: One may attend to saving life and to public needs on Shabbat,
and one may go to synagogues
to attend to communal affairs on Shabbat.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
One may go to theaters, circuses, and courthouses
phrases.notes: Public gathering places where government and community business was done.

phrases.english: to attend to communal affairs on Shabbat.
And the school of Menashe taught:
One may arrange matches for children to be betrothed on Shabbat,
and for a child, to arrange for him to learn to read
and to learn a trade?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִיבּוּר מִי אֲסִיר? וְהָא רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַב הַמְנוּנָא דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the bathroom/קריאת שמע tangent (steps 14-21) and returns to the rule of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that speaking about weekday matters is forbidden on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Many authorities allow talking about calculations, charity, community business, matches, and education on שבת. That seems to contradict a ban on weekday speech.

steps.title: Your business is forbidden; Heaven's business is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'חפצך' (your business). Only personal business talk is forbidden. Talk about מצוות and community needs, Heaven's business, is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'from pursuing your business and speaking a word.' Your business is forbidden. Heaven's business is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ban on speech covers only personal matters. All the examples in step 22 are מצוה matters, so they are allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק that forbids weekday speech says 'your business.' That word limits the ban to personal, worldly affairs. Charity, saving lives, community needs, matches, and teaching children are חפצי שמים, so speaking about them is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: On שבת, talking about personal weekday business is forbidden. Talking about מצוה and community matters (חפצי שמים) is permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for allowing pledges, communal planning, and arranging שידוכים and children's education on שבת.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'From pursuing your business and speaking a word'
Your business is forbidden,
Heaven's business is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: מִמְּצוֹא חֶפְצְךָ וְדַבֵּר דָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22 by narrowing the rule from step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule through the wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All weekday-style talk, including about מצוות, might be forbidden on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only personal business talk is forbidden. Talk about חפצי שמים is permitted.

steps.title: Calculations that are not your business or have no purpose are permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל rules that calculations of 'מלך' (none of your business) and 'מה בכך' (pointless) may be done on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Calculations that are 'what is it to you' and calculations that are 'what does it matter' may be calculated on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from שמואל about doing calculations on שבת. Some calculations are allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 taught that only 'חפצך', your own business, is forbidden. This ruling applies that idea to calculations. A calculation that has nothing to do with you (מלך) or has no practical result (מה בכך) is not 'your business,' so it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for 'מָה לָּךְ', meaning 'what is it to you?' It describes a calculation that has nothing to do with you.
'What does it matter?' It describes a calculation with no practical use.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the bracketed word as מֶלֶךְ (king). Here [מַלָּךְ] means 'מָה לָּךְ', 'what is it to you.'
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the שבת restriction on calculating depends on whether the calculation is truly your own business, the 'חפצך' idea from the פסוק.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Calculations of 'what is it to you'
phrases.notes: Calculations that have nothing to do with the person making them

phrases.english: and of 'what does it matter'
it is permitted to calculate them on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'חפצך' principle from Step 23 to calculations: calculations that are not your business are permitted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Calculations of מלך (irrelevant to the person) and מה בכך (of no practical use) are permitted on שבת.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the ruling: real past and future accounts are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that calculations about real past or future dealings are forbidden on שבת, and it begins to mention the permitted 'מלך' type.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: Calculations about things that already happened, or that will happen in the future, are forbidden to calculate. But calculations of 'what is it to you'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with שמואל. This passage stops in the middle of the ברייתא, right where it starts to list the permitted calculations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calculations about your real accounts, whether from the past or for the future, are 'your business,' so they are forbidden. The ברייתא then turns to 'של מלך' to say that calculations which are none of your business are permitted. This matches שמואל exactly. The rest of the sentence continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was also taught this way.' It introduces a ברייתא that supports the statement just made.
That will happen in the future

phrases.english: This was also taught:
Calculations about matters that have passed
or that will happen in the future
may not be calculated.
But those of 'what is it to you'...
phrases.notes: The ברייתא continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings ברייתא support for שמואל's ruling in Step 24.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that only calculations which are your own business are forbidden, while מלך calculations are permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא forbidding calculations about real past or future dealings and beginning to permit 'של מלך' calculations.
